_waveGeometry: *** CORRECTED FROM 6 TO 1. *** It was 6 because there are six methodology slots below, and that was the wrong question: `slotsInWaveSet` is how many slots run CONCURRENTLY, not how many exist. Every vector in this set targets ONE FB instance, ONE stimulus surface and ONE reset, so under D9's computed disjointness every pair of these slots conflicts and the colouring separates all six. The wave set is therefore SIX WAVES OF ONE SLOT, never one wave of six. Inferred from this submission's own vectors - the six slots share `HBA_Stim.*` inputs and `DB_Controls.FaultReset` throughout - and NOT verified against `ir/`, which this author is fenced from.
_whatMovedWhenItChanged: *** NOTHING. AND THE REASON IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIELD. *** GateCli computes slotsPerRead = MaxReadRegisters / resultRegistersPerSlot = 125 / 8 = 15, then readsPerCycle = ceil(slotsInWaveSet / slotsPerRead), then floor = readsPerCycle x RttP99Ms / ScanPeriodMs. Six slots at 8 result registers is 48 registers, which fits in ONE Modbus read, so ceil(6/15) and ceil(1/15) are both 1 and the floor is 8.6 scans either way - the floor is quantised on ROUND TRIPS, not on slot count. No window, no maxDurationScans, no wall-clock backstop and no gate-10a ceiling in this file was ever sized against six concurrent slots: every scan count here is derived from the register's bounds table (T#60S, T#2S) and the 23.33 ms scan period, and none of them has a term in slotsInWaveSet. At ONE slot the floor is exactly one round trip and cannot be anything else, whatever resultRegistersPerSlot says, so it is now insensitive to that field too.
_andTheDIRECTIONWasTheOtherWay: *** RAISED BECAUSE IT MATTERS MORE THAN THIS SUBMISSION. *** The instruction to recompute came with the reasoning that a floor derived from a wider wave than will ever run is TOO PERMISSIVE and fails toward reporting a missed assertion as a pass. For this arithmetic that is inverted: readsPerCycle is monotonically NON-DECREASING in slotsInWaveSet, and the floor is proportional to it, so over-declaring slots yields a floor that is too HIGH - windows must be LONGER to clear it, and gate 10a's sampled ceiling (window.PlantScans / floor) gets LOWER. Over-declaring was the conservative error in every place the number is consumed. The permissive direction is UNDER-declaring, which is what a submission would do by naming the slots it happens to be submitting rather than the wave set they will run in. Correcting 6 to 1 therefore RELAXES two gates rather than tightening them - by zero, here, because of the quantisation, but the sign is the thing to know.

represents: The commanded state of exactly three signals the monitored block consumes - the hopper high-level sensor, the FORWARD shredder running feedback, and the shared operator fault reset - injected at the input map's test members and at DB_Controls.FaultReset (FB_HopperBlockageStim N21; FC_Inputs N1 lines for Test[5]/Test[8]; FC_ControlMain N8 lines 91-93).

Presentation of that commanded state to the monitored block within the SAME scan it is computed: the model is called from Main N1, ahead of the input map (Main N2) and the control (Main N3), and it is called from no other block.

Six timeline shapes selected by the TENS digit of Profile (N7 DIV by 10), with segment boundaries accumulated from the commanded P1..P4 (N8): shape 1 hopper high and plant running throughout; shape 2 hopper high with the plant never running; shape 3 plant running throughout with the hopper low for [T1,T2); shape 4 hopper high throughout with the plant stopped for [T1,T2); shape 5 plant stopped for [T1,T4) with the hopper low for [T2,T3), i.e. the clear falls wholly inside the stop; shape 6 neither signal driven, hopper low and plant stopped (N11, N12, N13, N14).

A hopper clear of any commanded duration of one CPU scan or longer - including one deliberately SHORTER than the monitored block's clear-debounce filter time - as a stimulus, by choosing P2 (shape 3) or P3 (shape 5) (N8, N11).

A commanded operator reset in four modes (N16, N17): never asserted inside the scenario; one pulse of ResetPulseWidth = T#500MS at ScenarioT = ResetAt; continuously true for the whole scenario phase; one pulse of the same width at the model's own ModelThreshold value.

A fixed pre-scenario clear-down of T#5S in which the hopper is driven LOW and the plant driven STOPPED, containing a commanded reset asserted from T#3S to T#4S of the run (N4, N9 InCleardown, N16 ClearDownReset). This is a statement about what the model DRIVES, not about the state the monitored block ends up in.

A run that begins with NO clear-down at all - Offset = T#0S and InCleardown never true - whenever the retentive PreBoundaryDone is already set when the run latches (N5, N9). This is the form a run takes after an externally performed CPU stop/restart.

A pre-boundary conditioning interval in which the hopper is high AND the plant is running for the commanded PreBoundaryHighRunning, entered only when Precondition = 1 and PreBoundaryDone is clear (N9 InPreBoundary, N13, N14), ending in the latching of a single retentive Bool (N10). That Bool is the entire boundary mechanism the block contains.
A published observation window, Stim.Armed, true only while the scenario phase is running and only for ScenarioT in [ArmAt, ArmUntil) (N18), for arming observation latches outside this block.

A published, latched completion flag, Stim.ScenarioDone, set at ScenarioT >= EndAt (N19), which also drops the run latch (N1) and thereby leaves the hopper low and the plant stopped; it is re-armed only after the harness drops Start (N20).
A run that cannot be truncated by the harness dropping Start part-way through: Running seals itself and is broken only by ScenarioDone (N1).
Restoration of the field at the end of a run: the map's test-enable Test[0] follows Running (N21), so outside a run every mapped input is taken from its physical terminal again (FC_Inputs).
doesNotRepresent: Any physical or process behaviour of a hopper. There is no material, no level dynamics, no in-flight mass, no sensor noise and no coupling whatsoever between the plant-running signal and the hopper-level signal: both are computed from Shape and elapsed time alone (N13, N14). Shape 2 holds the hopper high with the plant stopped indefinitely and nothing in the block forbids a physically impossible combination.

An equipment-grounded model in the sense of spec S11 M2. The six shapes were fitted to the CASES THE SPECIFICATION AND VECTOR SET ASK FOR - the block's own comment says so ('six shapes cover every scenario the vector set asks for') - so the model inherits the register's assumptions and the register's blind spots are not represented by construction.

The field-side signal path. Values are injected at the input buffer's test members (N21), so DI5_SHR_RunFwdFB and DI8_HPR_LevelHigh are bypassed entirely (FC_Inputs N1). No wire break, stuck-at, contact bounce, DI hardware input filtering or terminal polarity is represented.

The REVERSE running feedback, or the plant-running condition as an OR of two directions. The model drives the forward feedback only and force-clears the reverse feedback's test member for the whole run (N22), while the monitored block's PlantRunning is Fwd OR Rev (FC_ControlMain line 92).

A coherent plant input image. DB_Input.Test[0] is the input map's SINGLE GLOBAL test-enable (FC_Inputs, every line), so while a run is under way EVERY member of DB_Input is taken from a Test bit - and only Test[5], Test[6] and Test[8] are written by anything in the corpus. The other nineteen read FALSE regardless of the field, so during a run the rest of the program (Control_Healthy, Cycle_Start/Stop, pusher limits, downstream running, motor fault, ...) sees an all-false input image. The model does not model those inputs; it suppresses them.

A reset private to the monitored block. N21 writes the SHARED DB_Controls.FaultReset, which FC_ControlMain fans out to the shredder sequencer (line 23), the motor system (line 39), the pusher (line 59), the monitored block (line 93) and the physical output DQ11_SHR_FaultReset (line 84). It is a plain coil evaluated every scan of the run, so it also overwrites any externally written operator reset for the duration.

A CPU stop, a CPU restart, or a power cycle. The block cannot command, cause, detect or confirm one. Nothing in it records that a restart occurred; the only thing it carries across is the single retentive Bool PreBoundaryDone (N10), which is set BEFORE any restart and says only that the pre-boundary phase completed.

A HELD pre-boundary wait for that restart - CONTRADICTS THE BLOCK'S OWN COMMENTS. InPreBoundaryWait requires NOT PreBoundaryDone (N9) and N10 sets PreBoundaryDone from InPreBoundaryWait, so the wait state is true for EXACTLY ONE SCAN (~2 ms) and can never be waited in. On the next scan Offset flips from ClearDownTime to T#0S (N5), so ScenarioT jumps forward by 5 s (N6), and either (a) EndAt <= PreBoundaryHighRunning + 5 s, in which case N19 latches ScenarioDone immediately and N20 RESETS THE RETAINED PreBoundaryDone in the same scan - the boundary marker is destroyed and the run ends - or (b) EndAt is larger, in which case the model resumes driving the scenario from a clock already 5 s + PreBoundaryHighRunning into a timeline whose segments T1..T4 are measured from zero. The model has no mechanism to zero its own scenario clock at the boundary; only the CPU restart, which clears the non-retentive Running and RunTimer, can do that. Consequence: the Precondition = 1 path delivers its intended scenario only if the CPU is stopped within the same scan the pre-boundary phase ends, and delivers nothing usable otherwise.

The monitored block's persistence threshold, or the instant it crosses it. ModelThreshold is a stimulus constant held as the instance start value T#60S (iDB_HopperBlockageStim) and is never read from the monitored block; ResetMode 3 places its pulse at the model's own number (N15, N16). If the block's preset differs, the pulse does not coincide with the block's crossing.

Any observation, expectation or judgement of the monitored block. No network of this block reads any member of iDB_HopperBlockageMonitor; Armed and ScenarioDone are published, never compared against anything.

The state the monitored block is actually in when a scenario starts. The clear-down drives the hopper low for 5 s and pulses the shared reset; whether that leaves the block unalarmed with a zeroed accumulator is the BLOCK'S behaviour, and this model neither establishes nor verifies it.

Sub-scan timing. Every phase boundary is a comparison against the run timer's ET sampled once per OB1 scan (N2, N3), so commanded transitions land on scan boundaries and two commanded transitions less than one scan apart collapse. The narrowest reset the model can command is T#500MS inside the scenario (N4 ResetPulseWidth) and 1 s inside the clear-down (N4 ClearResetFrom/ClearResetUntil).

Runs longer than the run timer. RunTimer's PT is T#10M (N2) and a TON's ET stops at PT, so RunT saturates at ten minutes and every phase comparison freezes with it: a run whose clear-down plus EndAt exceeds that never reaches EndAt, never publishes ScenarioDone, and never ends.

Validation of the commanded vector. Shape is Profile / 10 (N7); any Profile whose tens digit is not 1..5 - including 0, 6 and 7 or above - drives nothing at all and is indistinguishable in the driven signals from the deliberate idle shape 6. An unset or out-of-range command is a silent idle run, never a refusal.

More than one hopper clear or more than one plant stop per run. Each shape yields at most one clear interval and at most one stop interval (N11, N12), so a second high episode after a re-accumulation, a second clear, or repeated stop/start within one scenario is not representable in a single run.

An observation window that outlasts the scenario. Armed is ANDed with InScenario (N18), so an ArmUntil beyond EndAt is silently truncated at EndAt, and no ArmAt/ArmUntil window can open during the clear-down or the pre-boundary phase.

A run containing no operator reset at all. Every run that starts with a clear-down asserts the commanded reset from 3 s to 4 s of the run irrespective of ResetMode (N16, N17); ResetMode 0 means 'no reset inside the scenario', not 'no reset in this run'. ResetMode 2 likewise presents exactly ONE rising edge of the commanded reset - the reset is false from 4 s to 5 s of the run and true from the first scan of the scenario - not zero edges.

THE BLOCK'S OWN PRESET IS NOT READ, NOT KNOWN TO THIS AUTHOR, AND APPEARS NOWHERE IN THIS VECTOR. The budget from 60 s to 63 s: (a) +1.0 s for the clear-down handover. FB_HopperBlockageStim's clear-down is ClearDownTime = T#5S with its reset pulsed from T#3S to T#4S, so the pulse provably ENDS 1 s before ScenarioT = 0 and the episode really does start at zero - this second is headroom, not a needed allowance, and it is the SAME second VB-HBA-026a spends at the other end of the threshold (`ArmAtMs` 1000) for the same worry. Symmetry, not a new judgement. (b) +2.0 s for scan jitter and for the copy layer running one scan ahead of the block (contract 9.4) - VERBATIM the margin VB-HBA-026a uses below the threshold, at 2 s / 86 scans, and rig-proven at that size in two waves. Total 3 s = 129 scans = 5% of the threshold, against a requirement measured in one or two scans; the surplus is margin and is meant to be. *** WHAT THE OPEN COSTS AND WHAT IT BUYS, STATED BOTH WAYS BECAUSE IT CUTS BOTH: *** an effective threshold at or under 63 s reads true at every considered frame and PASSES - forgiven; one between 63 s and 75 s leaves early frames false and late frames true, which is where `temporalShape: throughout` earns its place (see `_observability`); one at or beyond 75 s is false at every considered frame and is a decisive Disagreed. The close is 75 s = `EndMs`: the model ANDs Armed with InScenario, so any `ArmUntilMs` beyond EndAt is silently truncated there anyway, and closing earlier would only forgive a later block. *** AND THE FIELD YOU ARE READING IS INVISIBLE TO THE GATE: see the finding on AMB-19 in the .md. ***
vectors._observability: *** THIS HALF IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL AND IT IS NOT DECORATION: without it, VB-HBA-026a's prohibition is satisfied perfectly by a block whose alarm output is DEAD, and the pair would be measuring uptime. *** It is Sampled rather than Latched because the claim is about a state that must be STANDING across the whole post-threshold window, not about an occurrence that must survive a poll gap; the assertion is a WHEN, so Sampled is admissible, and `ModesThatCanAnswer(PersistentState, When)` admits it. 514 scans is 12.0 s at 23.33 ms - ~60x the section 12a derivation 1 floor and ~5.4x the largest poll gap ever measured (2,216 ms, one sample in 2,000) - so the window cannot fall between polls. *** `temporalShape: throughout` IS DECLARED DELIBERATELY AND IT IS THE FIELD THAT MAKES THE 63 s BOUNDARY MEAN ANYTHING. *** `SeriesEvaluation` narrows the considered frames to those taken while `Stim.Armed` is high and then folds three ways: all agree is Held, none agree is Disagreed, and MIXED - some true, some false - is `Inconclusive` when the shape is `Unstated`. A block whose threshold lands inside 63-75 s produces exactly that mixed series, and an Inconclusive consumes a wave without deciding anything. Declared `throughout`, the same series becomes a universal claim contradicted by a named frame - an accusation instead of a shrug. The field is known to the gate's schema (`ExpectationDocument.TemporalShape`, so gate 0b accepts it rather than refusing the submission) and is wired end to end (GateCli builds the ObservabilityDeclaration with it; LoopRun passes it into the fold), and it widens what can be SAID, never what passes: a correct block agrees at every considered frame and returns Held with or without it. IT IS ON THIS EXPECTATION ONLY. VB-HBA-026a's expectation is `Latched`, which takes the latch-register path and never consults a shape - declaring one there would be a claim with no effect, which reads as checked and is not. *** WHAT A GREEN HERE DOES NOT LICENSE: *** this vector does not falsify the cited assertion. REQ-HBA-002:feecbe is a prohibition - 'does not assert at any point BEFORE the threshold' - and nothing observed after 63 s can contradict it. VB-HBA-026a is the half that can. A reader who takes this vector's green on its own has read it wrongly, and the same is true in the other direction.
